MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  FEBRUARY 18, 2020

  The Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at 7:00
  p.m. at City Council Chambers 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California
  by VICE CHAIR POPE

  1.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  VICE CHAIR POPE led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Pope, Bain, Romanelli, Ciarolla, McCormick, Retz

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Persichina

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager (ACM)
  Mike Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  Daniel A-Haja, Community Services Coordinator

  3.  COMMISSION ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA

  VICE CHAIR POPE presented a Plaque of recognition for his service as former Chair.

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF JANUARY 21, 2020

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER (ACM) DAVIS noted a misspelling of Mr. Mohr’s name in
  Item 5 and a missing name to the report.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  JANUARY 21, 2020 AS CORRECTED.

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 18, 2020
   7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT DRAFT SURVEY

  ACM DAVIS provided a brief overview per the agenda material.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated it would be worth clarifying if the classes have fees or not.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested editing the portion that asked “How many
  events have you participated in this year” to “Which events have you attended this year”.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ suggested checking off the events that have been attended
  instead to simplify the form.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked what prompted the survey.

  ACM DAVIS responded that City staff wanted to improve community outreach and to
  understand the community’s interests further. The survey will also help in setting future
  budgets for items of interest to the City. This survey will also serve as a baseline for
  community outreach.

  COMMISSIONER POPE noted that no question regarding City trails were in the survey
  and should be added. ACM DAVIS noted a section on trails will be added.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked why the age ranges were chosen. ACM DAVIS
  responded that the City was looking for age-specific interest of the City. COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK wanted to know why the age ranges varied. ACM DAVIS noted that they
  can be reevaluated.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that some individuals may not want their information used
  for other purposes than the survey and that this should be made aware to the participant.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked how this survey will be distributed to residents.
  ACM DAVIS responded that an electronic version and hard copies will be available and
  that local homeowners’ associations will be notified. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI
  asked if this survey would be mailed out and if it could be sent with the yearly City
  Celebration letter to residents.  ACM DAVIS said that should be considered.
  COMMISSIONER RETZ suggested handing out the survey at local City events.

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  B.  PROPOSED MULTI-USE WATERING STATION

  MAINTENANCE SUPERVISOR GOLDSMITH provided a brief overview per the agenda
  material.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if the stations can have a water fountain for humans as
  well as the bottle filler, pet level, and horse level. SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH will
  look into the matter.

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 18, 2020
   COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the bench and hitching post would be a separate
  staff item or if it will be included with the report to City Council. SUPERINTENDENT
  GOLDSMITH responded that it will be included and that the location is 25 feet wide and
  would be an ideal location near Kelley’s Corner and nearby school running clubs and
  events such as the annual Poker Ride. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the costs
  associated with the bench and hitching post may not be covered by Cal Water or if
  financing will need to be discussed before taking it to City Council. SUPERINTENDENT
  GOLDSMITH responded that the cost of the bench and hitching post would cost
  approximately $500. COMMISSIONER POPE asked if this would include the Eagle Scout
  project cost and SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH answered affirmatively. ACM DAVIS
  noted although it was not formally budgeted, it will be considered in future Scout projects.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked what funds this project will be using. ACM DAVIS
  responded that Pepper Tree Foundation or Quimby Funds can be used to pay for the
  Eagle Scout projects.  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggested to modify the
  recommendation which separates the two projects. ACM DAVIS noted they can be
  approved in two separate actions for City Council. COMMISSIONER POPE stated it can
  be an amendment to clarify the separate project in the recommendation.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the fountain does not have a water bottler filling station and
  a model should be selected to reflect that. She also asked about maintenance of the
  fountains. SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH responded that minor issues such as
  cracked hoses that can be maintained by City Staff for no additional cost.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to:

  APPROVE THE PROPOSED MULTI-USE WATERING STATION WITH STAFF
  RECOMMENDATION FOR CITY COUNCIL APPROVAL WITH MODIFICATIONS
  TO INCLUDE A DRINKING FOUNTAIN FOR HUMANS AND TO APPROVE THE
  PROPOSAL BY THE CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE TO BUILD THE STATION
  AT THEIR COST; TO APPROVE THE MAINTENANCE COST WHICH HIS
  ANTICIPATED TO BE $30 PER MONTH; AND TO APPROVE A PROPOSAL TO
  CONSIDER INSTALLING A BENCH AND HITCHING POST THROUGH AN
  EAGLE SCOUT PROJECT THAT WOULD BE APPROVED FOR UP TO $500 IF
  APPROVED BY THE COMMISSION AT A FUTURE DATE.

  CHAIR RETZ REQUESTED A ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Ciarolla, Bain, McCormick, Retz, Pope, & Romanelli
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Persichina

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  C.  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT PRIORITY LIST
  ACM DAVIS provided a brief overview per the agenda material.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if the scenic corridor on Palos Verdes Drive North could
  have the telephone lines buried. ACM DAVIS replied that the Hazard Mitigation plan will

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 18, 2020
   allow for access to future grants which may fund that project. COMMISSIONRE RETZ
  also noted the center median beautification project on PV Drive North is not completed
  and should be added to the list. ACM DAVIS noted that a future Master Landscape Plan
  will be discussed at the upcoming City Council Policy Development session.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the description would address the fencing repair,
  drainage, and water fountains as part of the $40,000 of the grant. ACM DAVIS stated that
  the $40,000 grant is specific to the fencing, but the additional items can be added to the
  list. COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that the park may have a leaky pipe due to water
  pooling in low points creating muddy areas in the park. SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH
  noted these observations and will look into it further. He also stated that a contractor will
  be meeting with him this week to look at the fencing at Highridge Park.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the status of Taber Grove. ACM DAVIS explained
  that although the initial phase of the project was approved by the Commission and City
  Council, the item is likely to return for review as the initial donation is not meeting the
  scope as proposed.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the tennis club bleachers project is a carry-over
  from a previous year as the bleachers are not used throughout the year even for the annual
  tennis tournament. ACM DAVIS replied that it can be reassessed and taken off the plan
  if needed.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the City Hall Chamber renovations were in the purview
  of the Commission. ACM DAVIS responded that the Chamber can serve as a community
  room and available to non-profit groups with public restrooms for nearby Chandler Park,
  which can use Quimby funds for parts of the renovation. The proposed renovations
  include plumbing and lighting and removal of the concrete stage in the room. Quimby
  funds are a part of it and other funds such as PEG fees can be used due to the
  broadcasting taking place in the Chambers. COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that the
  Chambers are used consistently but by fewer people than the parks and that funds would
  be better allocated towards parks. ACM DAVIS noted that it was a list for the City Council
  to review as part of their policy. The project was initially approved during the City Hall
  renovation but was later dropped from the scope and will be revisited by the City Council
  in March. The proposed projects would be completed in future years. The projects on
  the second page of the staff report are projected to be completed sooner such as replacing
  Rockbluff Park’s playground.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if the Butcher Park budget was still at $100,000
  and if it was going to be paid by the Metropolitan Water District (MWD) as it was proposed
  to be almost double that amount. ACM DAVIS stated that the budget was at $100,000
  and that MWD would indeed cover that cost. The increased cost may have been attributed
  to the expanded scope of the renovation which includes street work but this will be
  confirmed with the Public Works Director. COMMSSIONER MCCORMICK also asked
  about the status of the George F Canyon fence and asked if it would be budgeted as well.
  SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH noted that cost would be nominal and not needed to
  be on the list. COMMISSIONER MCCCORMICK also noted the volleyball court at Ernie
  Howlett Park needs to be remodeled or replaced with plants or outdoor workout stations.
  ACM DAVIS responded that a 2014 grant allowed for outdoor workout stations and

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 18, 2020
   grading of the surrounding park trail and that the volleyball court can be added to the list
  for future consideration.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted that three posts at Chandler Park are falling down on
  the east corner. SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH noted that it is slated for repair for a
  Scout Project but it will be inspected again for safety.

  COMMSIONER RETZ noted that the Dapplegray Park sign is in need of work as the “No
  Lunging” sign has the “no” portion worn off.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the Highridge Park water fountains have low pressure and
  another is full of weeds. There are also erosion and drainage issues that need to be looked
  at but the fields look well and free of gophers.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if the poison oak near the George F canyon nature
  pathway was cleared. SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH responded it was cleared.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted the trail by Dapplegray School looks well maintained.

  9.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA reported that letters have been sent
  out to local dignitaries inviting them to join the event. Rider turnout is expected to remain
  the same as last year.

  B.  CENTENNIAL CELEBRATION – WOMEN’S SUFFRAGE MARCH (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM DAVIS stated that the Palos Verdes Library District is putting on a replica women’s
  march on Saturday, March 14, 2020 which takes place from the library to the mall. The
  City will provide a sound system for the event. E-blasts and other notifications will be
  made for the event and minimal street closure will be made. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA
  asked if this is promoted by the schools as well. ACM DAVIS will ask if this will be done
  and make sure the proper avenues will be addressed. VICE CHAIR POPE asked if there
  would be a street closure for the event. ACM DAVIS noted that it would be a temporary
  lane closure with a Sheriff on hand to control traffic on Deep Valley Drive.

  10.  MATTER OF INFORMATION

  A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF JANUARY 27, 2020

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to:

  Receive and file.

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 18, 2020
   B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JANUARY 28, 2020

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to:

  Receive and file.

  C.  2019 PENINSULA PARADE OF LIGHTS DEBRIEF

  ACM DAVIS stated that the event was an overall success and an estimated 5,000
  spectators were in attendance. Due to the threat of rain, some parade groups did not
  participate which affected the order of the parade, but was unnoticed by the spectators.
  The live streaming was unsuccessful due to the increased cellular usage from the
  spectators during the event. The Parade Grand Marshall Allison Compton was well
  received though the Community Grand Marshalls Mr. and Mrs. Hill were not able to attend
  due to illness and may be invited back next year. Dale Allen enjoyed his time on the
  tractor float during the parade. The parade had 210 units which was a little over last year.
  Access to the parade route was difficult this year due to Cal Water’s work on Crenshaw
  Boulevard. Sheriff’s responded in a timely manner to a wrong-way driver which did not
  affect the safety of the parade itself. The parade ended on time and the awards ceremony
  and viewing area were well received. Promotions were the same as last year with new
  sponsorship options such as video promotions. The VIP area was well stocked and the
  Manhattan Beach studios had minor suggestions for next year’s event. The 2020 date is
  scheduled for Saturday, December 5.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI liked the indoor pre-parade reception and recommends
  having it indoors next year as well.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggests a snow machine next year, either at the mall
  of Ernie Howlett Park.

  VICE CHAIR POPE noted an empty spot on Beechgate due to poor lighting and suggested
  a possible food truck to attract spectators to the area. ACM DAVIS suggested local
  restaurant host a food truck in that area.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested adding a donation box for the event next year and
  suggested organizing this with another entity or co-promoting with other entities already
  accepting donations.

  COMMISIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to:

  Receive and file.

  D.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNEMNT GENERAL ASSEMBLY

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI had some trouble registering for the assembly. VICE
  CHAIR POPE wanted to know if she has registered and recommends newer members to
  take part.

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
FEBRUARY 18, 2020
   COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK
  to:

  Receive and file.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PARK REGULATIONS AMENDED MUNICIPAL CODE

  ACM DAVIS noted that staff is finalizing the Code with help from COMMISSIONER RETZ
  and the CITY ATTORNEY. COMMISSIONER RETZ will provide a finalized copy for the
  COMMSSION to review.

  B.  RECREATION FEE REVIEW

  ACM DAVIS noted staff is doing surveys and research on the fees and will coordinate with
  the new special event code.

  C.  SPECIAL EVENT FEE REVIEW

  ACM DAVIS noted this item will be presented in March

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if there is a deadline for the Conflict of Interest form. ACM
  DAVIS noted April 1st would be the deadline.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  VICE CHAIR POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 8:04 PM TO AN ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON MARCH 16, 2020 AT 7:00 P.M. IN THE CITY COUNCIL
  CHAMBER, 4045 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES.

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Alexa Davis
  Community Services Coordinator  Assistant City Manager

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
FEBRUARY 18, 2020
